phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm
phrases.ar: الٓمٓ
phrases.explanation: This verse consists of three letters, Alif, Lam and Mim, each pronounced separately, standing alone as the opening of the chapter. The commentary does not explain them here, because their full exposition was already given where the same letters first occur, at the head of the second chapter, and what was said there applies here in full, so it is referred back to rather than repeated. The same is done with the word that opens the next verse: the name Allah has likewise already been explained earlier, and is not glossed again here. The chapter therefore begins by pointing the reader back to the earlier discussion, and anyone who wants the meanings of the opening letters, and of the name Allah, will find them set out in full at those earlier occurrences.

phrases.translation: Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining
phrases.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُ
phrases.explanation:
The opening words, there is no god but He, announce that divinity belongs to Allah alone, to the exclusion of every other god or partner, and that worship is fitting for no one besides Him. Everything besides Him is His creation and His possession, He has no partner in His dominion, and whatever is worshipped besides Him belongs to its Creator and owes its obedience to Him. The verse argues against those who took partners with Him, and warns anyone who worshipped an idol, the sun, the moon, a person or an angel that he is in error and has strayed. It is reported to have been revealed concerning the Christian delegation of Najran, who claimed for Jesus that he is Allah, the son of Allah, or the third of three, and the Quran records their claims.

The Ever-Living describes Allah. The reciters differed over the vocalization: most read it al-hayy al-qayyum, while al-hayyu l-qayyum is reported from two of the companions and another early reciter. The preferred reading is al-hayy al-qayyum, the widespread reading established in the copies of the reciters of the Muslims. On the meaning of the Living, the exegetes differed: some said it means perpetual subsistence, denying of Allah the death possible to every other creature, while others said it means that for Him the governing of whatever He wills is easy and nothing is impossible for Him, unlike false gods without power. The preferred view is the abiding life that knows no perishing or interruption, because whoever dies and perishes cannot deserve to be worshipped, while the God is the one who abides and does not die.

On the Sustainer, the variant readings lie close in meaning: the one who guards, sustains, governs and disposes of all things as He wills. Some took it to mean the abiding in His place, denying only change of place and the alternation among creatures. The preferred view is that Allah sustains the affair of all things, warding off harm, guarding, governing and disposing of them by His power, in the idiom of one who manages the affair of a town. The word is built from the verb meaning to stand.

phrases.translation: He has revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ the Book in truth, confirming what came before it, as He revealed the Torah and the Gospel
phrases.ar: نَزَّلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ مُصَدِّقٗا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ وَأَنزَلَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةَ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلَ
phrases.explanation: The verse says Allah sent down the Book to the Prophet with the truth, and by the Book is meant the Quran, sent down to settle the matters over which the people of the Torah and the Gospel and the Christians of Najran differed. Confirming what came before it means the Quran confirms the earlier books sent down to the prophets and messengers of Allah, since the One who sent down all of them is One and there can be no contradiction in them, and had they come from other than Him there would be much contradiction. He also sent down the Torah to Moses and the Gospel to Jesus, as guidance for people, an exposition of the matters over which they differed about the oneness of Allah and the affirmation of His messengers.

phrases.translation: previously, as a guide for people, and ˹also˺ revealed the Standard ˹to distinguish between right and wrong˺.
phrases.ar: مِن قَبۡلُ هُدٗى لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَنزَلَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانَۗ
phrases.explanation: The verse begins with the words previously, as a guide for people, which the passage joins to the sending down of the Standard, and it then explains the Standard. The exegetes differed over its meaning here: one view takes it as the separation between truth and falsehood over which the parties of the various communities disagreed in the matter of Jesus and in other matters. The preferred view is that the Standard is the separation which Allah brought about between His Prophet and those who disputed with him over Jesus and his other affairs, through the conclusive proof that cut off their excuse and that of other disbelievers in Allah.

phrases.translation: Surely those who reject Allah’s revelations will suffer a severe torment. For Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٞ شَدِيدٞۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٞ ذُو ٱنتِقَامٍ
phrases.explanation: Surely those who reject the signs of Allah will suffer a severe torment, and Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment. By those who reject the signs are meant those who denied Allah's proofs of His oneness and His divinity, denied that Jesus is His servant, and took the Messiah as a god and lord or claimed a son for Allah: for them is a severe punishment. The passage adds that whoever denies that separation between right and wrong faces a severe punishment, a threat against whoever opposes the truth after it has become clear to him. Allah is Almighty in His sovereignty, so no one can prevent Him from punishing whom He wills, and He is the Lord of retribution against whoever denied His arguments after they were established and became clear to him.

phrases.translation: Surely nothing on earth or in the heavens is hidden from Allah
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ شَيۡءٞ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ
phrases.explanation: Surely nothing on earth or in the heavens is hidden from Allah. The passage explains that by this Allah means that nothing that is on the earth is hidden from Him, and nothing that is in the heaven is hidden from Him either. It then turns to those who dispute with the Prophet over the signs of Allah, namely the Christians of Najran in what they claim about Jesus son of Mary: how could their false pretense about him remain hidden from Him, who is the Knower of all things. Their claim about Jesus is not concealed from Allah, who knows what is hidden and what is manifest, so their pretense cannot stand before Him.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who shapes you in the wombs of your mothers as He wills. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ كَيۡفَ يَشَآءُۚ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
phrases.explanation: He is the One Who shapes you in the wombs of your mothers as He wills. The passage explains that Allah shapes and forms you in your mothers' wombs as He wills, making this one a man and that one a woman, this one black and that one red. By this He shows His servants that everyone enclosed in a womb is among those He shaped and created as He willed, including Jesus son of Mary, whom He shaped in his mother's womb. Had he been a god, he would not be enclosed in a womb, for the Creator of what is in the wombs cannot Himself be enclosed in one: wombs enclose only the created. The verse then declares that there is no god but He, the Almighty, the All-Wise.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who has revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ the Book, of which some verses are precise—they are the foundation of the Book—while others are elusive. Those with deviant hearts follow the elusive verses seeking ˹to spread˺ doubt through their ˹false˺ interpretations—but none grasps their ˹full˺ meaning except Allah. As for those well-grounded in knowledge, they say, “We believe in this ˹Quran˺—it is all from our Lord.” But none will be mindful ˹of this˺ except people of reason
phrases.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَٰتٞ مُّحۡكَمَٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتٞۖ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ زَيۡغٞ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنۡهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ تَأۡوِيلِهِۦۖ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ تَأۡوِيلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُۗ وَٱلرَّٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلّٞ مِّنۡ عِندِ رَبِّنَاۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
phrases.explanation:
He revealed the Book to the Prophet, and by the Book is meant the Quran. Of its verses some are precise, the foundation of the Book, and others elusive. Elusive means ambiguous in recitation and differing in meaning, like things resembling one another in appearance while their kinds differ. The precise are those Allah clarified, the foundation of the religion of the Prophet and his community and their refuge in the ordinances of Islam.

The exegetes differed over the precise and the elusive. Some said the precise are the verses put into practice that establish rulings, and the elusive the abrogated ones. Others said the precise clarify the permitted and the forbidden, the elusive resemble one another in meaning though wordings differ. Others said the precise admit one interpretation, the elusive several. Others said the precise are the verses and the stories of past nations, the elusive the repeated stories with agreeing wordings but differing meanings. On the foundation of the Book, some said the obligations, punishments and rulings, others the opening letters of the chapters.

As for those in whose hearts is deviation: an inclination away from the truth and straying from it, the deviation the believers pray against in the next verse. Such hearts follow the elusive verses, whose wordings resemble and meanings branch, to claim false readings and mislead the weak. The exegetes differed over whom it means: some said the Christian delegation of Najran, who disputed over Jesus, others a party of Jews who disputed over the duration of the Prophet's rule through the disjoined letters, others every religious innovator who contradicts the Messenger through his reading of them. The preferred view is those who disputed with the Messenger by means of the ambiguous, whether over Jesus or over the duration of his rule.

On seeking doubt, some said striving after ascribing partners to Allah, others striving after ambiguities, and the more correct is the desire for ambiguities and misleading: the deviant follow ambiguous verses to mislead themselves and others, invoking falsehood instead of the clarified truth. The verse applies to every innovator who disputed over the ambiguous and turned from the precise verses, and a report adds: when you see those who dispute about it, they are the ones Allah meant, so beware of them. On seeking its interpretation, some said the term the Jews sought by reckoning the disjoined letters, others the reading of the ambiguous according to their deviant hearts.

None knows its interpretation but Allah means none knows the coming of the Hour, the end of the duration of the Prophet's rule and his community, and what will come to pass, but Allah alone, excluding those who hoped to learn it by reckoning, astrology and soothsaying. The exegetes differed on the grammar: some conjoined the firmly rooted with Allah so that they too know the interpretation, while the firmly rooted say we believe in it, and others made them a new subject affirming belief in the ambiguous and that only Allah knows its interpretation. The firmly rooted affirm the ambiguous is truth though its interpretation is unknown to them, and that the whole Book is from their Lord. None will be mindful but people of reason: only those with understanding are restrained from speaking of the ambiguous without knowledge.

phrases.translation: ˹They say,˺ “Our Lord! Do not let our hearts deviate after you have guided us. Grant us Your mercy. You are indeed the Giver ˹of all bounties˺
phrases.ar: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغۡ قُلُوبَنَا بَعۡدَ إِذۡ هَدَيۡتَنَا وَهَبۡ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحۡمَةًۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡوَهَّابُ
phrases.explanation: Our Lord! Do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself, for You are the Giver. The passage says this is the prayer of those firmly rooted in knowledge. By let not our hearts deviate they mean: do not incline our hearts away from Your guidance after guiding us, nor make us like those whose hearts deviated and followed the ambiguous verses seeking sedition and an interpretation none knows but Allah. By grant us mercy they mean steadfastness in affirming the Book, and by the Giver the One who bestows right guidance to steadfastness upon His religion. The passage adds that this praised prayer refutes the claim that making a heart deviate would be injustice from Allah, who does no injustice to His servants.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! You will certainly gather all humanity for the ˹promised˺ Day—about which there is no doubt. Surely Allah does not break His promise.”
phrases.ar: رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ ٱلنَّاسِ لِيَوۡمٖ لَّا رَيۡبَ فِيهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُخۡلِفُ ٱلۡمِيعَادَ
phrases.explanation: Our Lord! You will certainly gather all humanity for the promised Day, about which there is no doubt. Surely Allah does not break His promise. The passage says this too is said by those firmly rooted in knowledge. The sentence carries an unstated request: gather mankind for the Day of Resurrection, so forgive us and pardon us on that Day, for You do not break Your promise to forgive whoever believes in You, follows Your Messenger and acts by Your Book. By for a Day is meant on a Day, the day of gathering for the decisive judgment, at the place of presentation and reckoning. The Day about which there is no doubt is the Day of Resurrection, already expounded earlier. And the promise is the word built from the root meaning a promise.

phrases.translation: Indeed, neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah—and they will be the fuel for the Fire
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن تُغۡنِيَ عَنۡهُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـٔٗاۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمۡ وَقُودُ ٱلنَّارِ
phrases.explanation: Indeed, neither the wealth nor the children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah, and they will be the fuel for the Fire. By those who disbelieve are meant those who denied the truth they had already recognized, the prophethood of the Prophet, among the Jews and their hypocrites, and the hypocrites and disbelievers among the Arabs whose hearts had deviated and who followed the elusive verses of the Book seeking doubt. By neither their possessions nor their children will avail them He means that neither will save them from the punishment of Allah when it befalls them, neither in this world, where they are punished at once for denying the truth after it became clear to them, nor in the Hereafter, where they are the firewood of the Fire.

phrases.translation: Their fate will be like that of the people of Pharaoh and those before them—they all rejected Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in punishment
phrases.ar: كَدَأۡبِ ءَالِ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
phrases.explanation: Their fate will be like that of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they all rejected Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins, and Allah is severe in punishment. The passage explains that those who disbelieve will find that neither their possessions nor their children avail them anything against Allah when Our punishment befalls them, just as was the constant practice of Pharaoh's people and the custom of the nations before them, who denied Our signs and were seized on account of their sins and destroyed, so that neither possessions nor children availed them when the severe punishment came upon them. It names earlier peoples hastened to punishment for denying their Lord before Pharaoh's people: the people of Noah, of Hud, of Lot, and their like. The exegetes differed over the word for their fate being like that of Pharaoh's people: some said like their constant practice, some like their deed, others like their denial. And Allah is severe in punishment means He is severe in punishing whoever disbelieved in Him and denied His messengers after the proof was established against him.

phrases.translation: ˹O Prophet!˺ Tell the disbelievers, “Soon you will be overpowered and driven to Hell—what an evil place to rest!”
phrases.ar: قُل لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَتُغۡلَبُونَ وَتُحۡشَرُونَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمِهَادُ
phrases.explanation: Say to the disbelievers: soon you will be overpowered and driven to Hell, what an evil place to rest. The reciters differed over this verse: a group of the reciters of Kufa read you shall be overcome as they shall be overcome and they shall be driven together, taking it to mean that the Arab polytheists shall be overcome, in an address to the Jews. The preferred reading is with you, in the meaning: say to those who disbelieve among the Jews, who follow the elusive verses of the Book seeking doubt and its interpretation, that they shall be overcome and driven together to Hell, and how wretched is that resting place. The reports indicate the addressees are the Jews mentioned in the previous verse, which shows the reading with you is more fitting. And driven together means gathered and conveyed to Hell.

phrases.translation: Indeed, there was a sign for you in the two armies that met in battle—one fighting for the cause of Allah and the other in denial.
phrases.ar: قَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ ءَايَةٞ فِي فِئَتَيۡنِ ٱلۡتَقَتَاۖ فِئَةٞ تُقَٰتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَأُخۡرَىٰ كَافِرَةٞ
phrases.explanation: Indeed, there was a sign for you in the two armies that met in battle, one fighting for the cause of Allah and the other in denial. The passage tells the disbelieving Jews that there was indeed for them a sign, a token and an indication of the truth of what is said, that they will be overcome, and a lesson. In two hosts means two groups and parties, a host being a multitude of people, and that met means for battle. One of the two hosts was the Messenger and those with him at the battle of Badr, and the other was the polytheists of Quraysh. The repeated word may be read in either case, and the genitive is permissible in the word for a host as a reference back to in two hosts that met, but the reading is not permitted because the authoritative reciters agree on the contrary. The reciters differed over who saw whom: the reciters of Medina read you see them, meaning you Jews see the polytheists as twice the Muslims, and most of the reciters of Kufa and Basra and some of Mecca read they see them, meaning the Muslims see the disbelieving multitude as twice the Muslims. The exegetes differed over which host saw the other doubled: some said the Muslim host saw the polytheists as twice its own number, Allah diminishing them in their eyes, others said Allah showed the disbelieving host the Muslims as twice their own. The preferred reading is they see them, the Muslims seeing the disbelievers as twice themselves, because Allah diminished the enemy in their eyes in stages. Reports also differed over the number of the polytheists at Badr, some saying a thousand, some nine hundred to a thousand, contradicting the report of a companion that their number exceeded nine hundred, so the exposition resting on the other companion's report is the most suitable.

phrases.translation: The believers saw their enemy twice their number. But Allah supports with His victory whoever He wills. Surely in this is a lesson for people of insight
phrases.ar: يَرَوۡنَهُم مِّثۡلَيۡهِمۡ رَأۡيَ ٱلۡعَيۡنِۚ وَٱللَّهُ يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصۡرِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَعِبۡرَةٗ لِّأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
phrases.explanation: The believers saw their enemy twice their number by the eye. By the seeing of the eye is meant what the eye perceives where the gaze falls, and the meaning is that they saw the enemy as twice themselves in number. But Allah supports with His victory whoever He wills: to support means to strengthen and aid, from the saying I supported someone, and the verse recalls the servant David, the possessor of strength. The exposition runs: there was for you, O Jews, in two hosts that met, one fighting in the way of Allah and another disbelieving, whom the Muslims saw as twice themselves with their own eyes, whereupon We supported the Muslim host, small in number, against the disbelieving host, abundant in number, until they prevailed over them. Surely in this is a lesson for people of insight: in that means in what We did with those described, Our support of the small Muslim host against the abundant disbelieving one, there is something to ponder over and an admonition for whoever has understanding, takes heed and thereby perceives the truth. The passage adds that Allah let the Jews know the differing states in which the Muslims saw the enemy's number, as a communication from Him that He supports the believers with His aid, so that they should not be deluded by the enemy's numbers and fighting prowess, and should beware lest the same chastisement that befell the Quraysh at Badr should befall them at the hands of the believers.

phrases.translation: The enjoyment of ˹worldly˺ desires—women, children,
phrases.ar: زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلۡبَنِينَ
phrases.explanation: The enjoyment of worldly desires, women and children, has been made appealing to people. The passage explains that what is made fair and attractive to mankind is the love of what they desire, women, sons and all the rest that is enumerated, the love of it being beautified in their eyes while they live in the world, so that they prefer it over what endures. In saying this He intended a rebuke of the Jews, who preferred the worldly life and the love of leadership in it over following the Prophet, after they had come to know his truthfulness, choosing the perishable enjoyment of this world over the lasting good that is with their Lord.

phrases.translation: treasures of gold and silver,
phrases.ar: وَٱلۡقَنَٰطِيرِ ٱلۡمُقَنطَرَةِ مِنَ ٱلذَّهَبِ وَٱلۡفِضَّةِ
phrases.explanation: Treasures of gold and silver are of the same love of desires, heaped up in hoards, the hoards being the plural of a single hoard. On the value of the qintar, the exegetes differed widely, and each side supported its view with reports, some of which trace the figures to the Prophet and to the early generations. Some said it is twelve hundred uqiya, an uqiya being a measure of weight. Others said it is twelve hundred dinars, the gold coin, and of silver twelve hundred mithqal, a weight of gold. Others said twelve thousand dirhams, the silver coin, or one thousand dinars, and one of these added that a thousand dinars is the blood-money of one of you. Others said eighty thousand dirhams, or a hundred ratl, a pound, of gold. Others said simply seventy thousand, without naming the unit. Others pictured it as the hide of a bull filled with gold. Others said the word means abundant wealth outright. And others took the second word of the phrase to mean minted, that is, coined into dirhams and dinars. That the views run through every measure in use, weight and coin alike, is itself the sign that the word points to abundance rather than a fixed sum. The preferred view is that one says the qintar is abundant wealth, whose weight is not fixed arbitrarily with a bound, because if its quantity had been delimited among them, there would not have been all this disagreement among the earlier exegetes about it, and whatever more has been said of it is only what was transmitted. The hoard is what is piled up and heaped, and the verse joins the hoards to gold and silver.

phrases.translation: fine horses,
phrases.ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلِ ٱلۡمُسَوَّمَةِ
phrases.explanation: Fine horses are made appealing too. On the marked horses, the exegetes differed: some said those that graze and pasture, others the beautiful ones, others horses bearing a mark or brand as a sign, and others horses prepared for fighting in the path of Allah. The preferred view is that they are the horses marked with coloring patterns, the beautiful ones whose beauty enchants whoever sees them, because marking in the language of the Arabs is the taswim, the brand being the wasm, and Allah marked the beautiful horses with beauty in their colors, their coloring patterns and their forms, so they are also the well formed and the enchanting, which is one and the same meaning. To this belong the descriptions of horses in the poetry of the Arabs, where a poet of the Banu Dhubyan and another poet used this very word. The grazing reading is set aside, because in their language this word is not used for setting animals to pasture, for that one says another word, while the livestock that grazes by itself is called by another form, and the camel herder is called by another name. And the view that the horses are prepared for the path of Allah lies far from the meaning of the word, so directing the explanation to the marked is the more correct. Some explained the marking as the brand with which a horse is marked, and others as the beauty that sets it apart, and the correct of these statements is one description, the marked, the well formed and the enchanting together.

phrases.translation: cattle, and fertile land—has been made appealing to people.
phrases.ar: وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ وَٱلۡحَرۡثِۗ
phrases.explanation: Cattle and fertile land have been made appealing to people. On the cattle, the word is the plural of na'am and means the eight pairs that Allah named in His Book, two of each of the four kinds, of sheep, goats, oxen and camels, every grazing animal of those kinds. And the tillage is the cultivated land, the fields that are plowed and sown. The passage repeats that all of this is of the love of desires made attractive to mankind, perishable pleasures of the worldly life. The land yields its crop from the tilling, and both the cattle and the fields are among the enjoyments of the worldly life that the love of them beautifies for people.

phrases.translation: These are the pleasures of this worldly life,
phrases.ar: ذَٰلِكَ مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ
phrases.explanation: These are the pleasures of this worldly life. By the word that refers to them, the passage explains, He meant everything named in the verse together, women, sons, the hoards of gold and silver, the marked horses, the cattle and the tillage, showing that one word can encompass many matters of different meanings. And the enjoyment of the worldly life is a notice that all of that is enjoyed by the people of the world while they live, a means in their livelihood and an occasion for fulfilling their desires in their perishable world, without being a provision for the Hereafter or a means of nearness to their Lord, except what is spent in His path.

phrases.translation: but with Allah is the finest destination
phrases.ar: وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُۥ حُسۡنُ ٱلۡمَـَٔابِ
phrases.explanation: But with Allah is the finest destination. The good return means the good place of return, the word being a verbal noun on the pattern of maf'al from the saying of the man who returns, like the words for saying, promise and occasion. An objection is answered: how can it be said that with Allah is the good return, when with Him on that Day is the painful punishment and the severe retribution. The answer is that the good return is what Allah Himself described, namely the return to gardens beneath which the rivers flow, abiding in them eternally, and purified spouses and the good pleasure of Allah.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Shall I inform you of what is better than ˹all of˺ this? Those mindful ˹of Allah˺ will have Gardens with their Lord under which rivers flow,
phrases.ar: قُلۡ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُم بِخَيۡرٖ مِّن ذَٰلِكُمۡۖ لِلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ جَنَّٰتٞ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ
phrases.explanation: Say, shall I inform you of what is better than all of this? The passage addresses the people for whom the love of the desires of this world, women, sons, hoards of gold and silver and the possessions that are the perishable enjoyment of this world, has been made fair-seeming, and offers them something better and more excellent. The exegetes differed over where the questioning ends: some let it end at something better than that, so that what follows is a new statement about the gardens belonging to those mindful of Allah, with the gardens in the nominative, others ended it at with their Lord. The preferred view is that the questioning ends at something better than that.

phrases.translation: to stay there forever, and pure spouses, along with Allah’s pleasure.” And Allah is All-Seeing of ˹His˺ servants
phrases.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا وَأَزۡوَٰجٞ مُّطَهَّرَةٞ وَرِضۡوَٰنٞ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
phrases.explanation: To stay there forever, and pure spouses, along with Allah's pleasure, and Allah is All-Seeing of His servants. Those mindful of Allah are those who feared Him and obeyed Him by performing His obligations and avoiding disobedience. The gardens are orchards with rivers flowing beneath them, and abiding forever means perpetual continuance in them. The pure spouses are the women of Paradise purified of every affliction. The good pleasure of Allah is His contentment, and the passage notes that of all the good prepared for the God-fearing, Allah mentioned only His good pleasure, because it is the highest rank of the honors of Paradise. And Allah All-Seeing of the servants means He has insight into which of His servants fears Him, is wary of Him, obeys Him and prefers what is with Him.

phrases.translation: who pray, “Our Lord! We have believed, so forgive our sins and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”
phrases.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَآ ءَامَنَّا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
phrases.explanation: Who pray, Our Lord! We have believed, so forgive our sins and protect us from the torment of the Fire. This verse completes the previous one, which offers something better for those mindful of Allah, namely those who say this prayer. The words those who say may be read in the genitive, referring back to the God-fearing, or in the nominative as a new sentence at the head of the verse, and both readings are permissible. The prayer means: we have believed in You, in Your Prophet and in what he brought, so forgive us our sins, covering them over and refraining from punishing us for them, and protect us from the torment of the Fire, turning Your punishment away from us, which in reality means: do not punish us with the Fire.

phrases.translation: ˹It is they˺ who are patient, sincere, obedient, and charitable,
phrases.ar: ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ وَٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ وَٱلۡقَٰنِتِينَ وَٱلۡمُنفِقِينَ
phrases.explanation: It is they who are patient, sincere, obedient, and charitable. The patient are those who showed patience in adversity and hardship and at the moment of battle. The sincere are those who were truthful toward Allah in their word, affirming Him, His Messenger and what He brought, acting on what He commanded and refraining from what He forbade. The obedient are those who obey Him, and the charitable are those who spend. The full explanation of these words was given earlier, with proofs and reports, so it is not repeated here. Grammatically these words stand in the genitive, referred back to those who say, which is itself referred back to for those who are God-fearing.

phrases.translation: and who pray for forgiveness before dawn
phrases.ar: وَٱلۡمُسۡتَغۡفِرِينَ بِٱلۡأَسۡحَارِ
phrases.explanation: And who pray for forgiveness before dawn. By the last hours of the night is meant the end of the night, the hours before dawn, when the servant turns to his Lord alone. The exegetes differed over whom this description belongs to: some said it is those who pray in the last hours of the night, others said those who ask for forgiveness, and others said those who attend the dawn prayer in congregation, each side supporting its view with reports. The preferred view is that they are those who ask their Lord to cover over their disgrace and sins in those hours. On the asking itself, the clearest of its meanings is that their asking of Him takes place by supplication in the last hours of the night, and it is possible that it means their striving for His forgiveness by means of deeds and prayer, except that the clearest is the supplication mentioned.

phrases.translation: Allah ˹Himself˺ is a Witness that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—and so are the angels and people of knowledge. He is the Maintainer of justice.
phrases.ar: شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ قَآئِمَۢا بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۚ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا
phrases.explanation:
Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and likewise the angels and those who possess knowledge. In the grammar of the verse, the phrase for "that He" is in the accusative case because the verb "He bears witness" governs it, and "the angels" are conjoined to the name of Allah. Some scholars of Basra explained "Allah bears witness" as meaning "Allah has decreed," but this is rejected, for witnessing is a particular meaning and decreeing is something other than it.

The exegetes differed over the vowels. The reciters of the people of Islam read the first "that He" with a fatha and the second "indeed" with a kasra, beginning a new sentence, so that "He bears witness" governs the first "that He." Some later scholars of Arabic read both with a fatha, joining "indeed the religion with Allah is Islam" to the first "that He." The preferred view is the first, and what was attributed to the early reciters behind the other reading is unknown in any narration, sound or weak.

Others explained the vowels differently: that the first "indeed" stands as a cause, meaning Allah bears witness because He is One, or that it is a parenthetical insertion while the witnessing falls on the second "that He."

As for "while He upholds justice," this means that it is He who attends to equity among His creatures. The most correct view is that "upholding" describes Allah Himself as a circumstantial qualifier, because the angels and those with knowledge are conjoined to it. The verse was intended only to deny what the Christians ascribed to Allah regarding Jesus, that He has a son, and what the polytheists ascribed to Him, that He has a partner. Thus Allah began with Himself, glorifying Himself above what they ascribed to Him, just as He has made it a custom for His servants to begin with His remembrance.

phrases.translation: There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.ar: هُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
phrases.explanation: By "there is no god but He, the Almighty, the All-Wise," He means the denial that anything deserves worship apart from the One who has no partner in His sovereignty. By "the Almighty" He means the One for whom nothing He wills is impossible and whom no one can resist when He punishes or takes vengeance upon him, and by "the All-Wise" He means wisdom in His disposing of all affairs, so that no defect creeps into it. This is the testimony that He Himself, His angels, and those of His creatures who have knowledge all bear together, which is why the verse repeats it at its end.

phrases.translation: Certainly, Allah’s only Way is Islam. Those who were given the Scripture did not dispute ˹among themselves˺ out of mutual envy until knowledge came to them.
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡإِسۡلَٰمُۗ وَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡعِلۡمُ بَغۡيَۢا بَيۡنَهُمۡۗ
phrases.explanation:
By "indeed the religion with Allah is Islam," He means surrender through submission and humility, from the verb meaning to enter into peace: submission with humility and the abandonment of resistance. The obedience that is real obedience with Him is acknowledgement with tongue and heart of servitude and submission to Him, and humbling themselves before Him in what He commanded and forbade, without arrogance toward Him and without associating any of His creatures with Him.

By "those who were given the Book did not dispute among themselves except after knowledge came to them, out of mutual envy," He means the people of the Gospel, for the Gospel is the Book mentioned in this verse. They became divided over the matter of Jesus and fabricated lies against Allah, so that some of them held the blood of others permissible, only after knowledge had come to them and they were certain that what they claimed was error. They did not speak out of ignorance but out of transgression of one against another and the pursuit of leadership, kingship, and dominion.

phrases.translation: Whoever denies Allah’s signs, then surely Allah is swift in reckoning
phrases.ar: وَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
phrases.explanation: By "whoever denies Allah's signs, then surely Allah is swift in reckoning," He means whoever denies the proofs of Allah and His signs, which He has set up as an admonition for whoever has understanding and as indications for whoever takes a lesson from them. Allah scrupulously keeps account of the deeds a person performed in this world and will requite him for them in the hereafter. "Swift in the reckoning" means swift in the tallying: He preserves every deed against the one who did it without difficulty, without effort, and without counting on the fingers as people count on their palms. Whoever thus denies Him after the signs have reached him has no excuse left.

phrases.translation: So if they argue with you ˹O Prophet˺, say, “I have submitted myself to Allah, and so have my followers.”
phrases.ar: فَإِنۡ حَآجُّوكَ فَقُلۡ أَسۡلَمۡتُ وَجۡهِيَ لِلَّهِ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِۗ
phrases.explanation: So if they argue with you, say, I have submitted myself to Allah, and so have my followers. If the disputants are the Christians of Najran contending over Jesus with falsehood, say: I have submitted myself to Allah alone, with my tongue, my heart and all my limbs. The command singles out submitting my face to Allah because the face is the most honored of the limbs, holding a man's splendor and eminence, and when he humbles his face before something, the rest of his limbs, lower in honor, have already humbled themselves before it. And whoever follows me has submitted his face to Allah together with me, the word whoever being coupled to the first-person ending of I have submitted.

phrases.translation: And ask those who were given the Scripture and the illiterate ˹people˺,
phrases.ar: وَقُل لِّلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ
phrases.explanation: And ask those who were given the Scripture and the illiterate people, have you submitted yourselves to Allah? Those given the Book are the Jews and the Christians, and the unlettered are those among the Arab polytheists who have no Book. Have you submitted means: have you set apart the acknowledgment of oneness for Allah and devoted worship and veneration to the Lord of the worlds sincerely, to the exclusion of the partners you ascribe to Him, while you know there is no lord besides Him and no god except He. A question in this form can carry the force of a command or a request, as in will you then desist, or the request for a table from heaven, so a conditional answer is given to it just as to a command.

phrases.translation: “Have you submitted yourselves ˹to Allah˺?” If they submit, they will be ˹rightly˺ guided. But if they turn away, then your duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺. And Allah is All-Seeing of ˹His˺ servants
phrases.ar: ءَأَسۡلَمۡتُمۡۚ فَإِنۡ أَسۡلَمُواْ فَقَدِ ٱهۡتَدَواْۖ وَّإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَلَٰغُۗ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
phrases.explanation: If they submit, they will be rightly guided, that is, they have found the path of truth and walked the way of right guidance, having submitted to setting apart oneness for Allah and devoting worship to Him sincerely. But if they turn away in aversion from what you invite them to, Islam and sincere devotion to Allah, then your duty is only to deliver the message, and upon you rests nothing but conveying the message to those to whom I sent you and fulfilling what I charged you. And Allah is All-Seeing of His servants: He knows which of His servants accepts what I sent you with and obeys you through Islam, and which turns away from it and rejects it.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who deny Allah’s signs, kill the prophets unjustly,
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ
phrases.explanation: Indeed, those who deny Allah's signs and kill the prophets unjustly. Those who deny the signs are those who reject the proofs of Allah and dismiss His signs as falsehood, among the People of the two Books, the Torah and the Gospel. And kill the prophets without right means that they killed the messengers of Allah who came to them forbidding the acts of disobedience they were committing and the matters from which Allah had already restrained them in their books, such as Zechariah and his son John, and others like them. To kill without right is to kill although the right of the prophet was established and known to them. They are the people of the Torah and the Gospel.

phrases.translation: and kill people who stand up for justice—give
phrases.ar: وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ
phrases.explanation: And kill people who stand up for justice. The reciters differed over this clause: the majority of the reciters of the cities read and they kill those who enjoin justice, while some of the later reciters of Kufa read and they fight, relying on the copy of a companion. The preferred reading is and they kill, because the authoritative reciters agree upon it and the interpreters explain it thus. The verse means those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, kill the prophets without right, and kill those who enjoin upon them Allah's justice in His command and prohibition, those who restrain them from killing the prophets of Allah.

phrases.translation: them good news of a painful punishment
phrases.ar: فَبَشِّرۡهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
phrases.explanation: Give them good news of a painful punishment. The passage explains: inform them, O Prophet, and let them know that there is with Allah a punishment that is painful for them, the agonizing one. By give them good news He means: announce to them and make known to them, for the word for giving tidings is the word for announcing news. By a painful punishment He means the agonizing one, the punishment that inflicts the utmost pain. And the news announced to these people is that this is what awaits them with Allah for their disbelief in His signs and for killing the prophets and those who enjoined justice upon them.

phrases.translation: They are the ones whose deeds are wasted in this world and the Hereafter. And they will have no helpers
phrases.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَبِطَتۡ أَعۡمَٰلُهُمۡ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
phrases.explanation: They are the ones whose deeds are wasted in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers. By they are meant those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah. Their works coming to nothing means their works were annulled, here and in the Hereafter. In this world they gained no praise, for they were in error and falsehood: Allah raised no honorable mention for them but cursed them and exposed their disgrace through His prophets and books, an enduring reproach. In the Hereafter He has prepared the punishment described in His Book, and their works fall to nothing with no reward, being disbelief in Allah, and their recompense is everlasting abode in the blazing Fire. And no helpers means no one will help them against Allah when He avenges their crimes.

phrases.translation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scriptures? Yet when they are invited to the Book of Allah to settle their disputes, some of them turn away heedlessly
phrases.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ نَصِيبٗا مِّنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ يُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَىٰ كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ لِيَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّىٰ فَرِيقٞ مِّنۡهُمۡ وَهُم مُّعۡرِضُونَ
phrases.explanation: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scriptures, yet when invited to the Book of Allah to settle their disputes, some turn away heedlessly. The exegetes differed over which Book they were called to: some said the Torah, which they acknowledged, others the Book sent down to the Prophet, a group being called to the Messenger to judge between them but refusing. The preferred view: a group of the Jews of Medina were called to the Torah about a dispute with the Messenger, whether his prophethood, the religion of Abraham, Islam, or a prescribed punishment, and they refused its judgment, some concealing it. Turning away averse means turning one's back on the Book one was called to, knowing its reality and proof.

phrases.translation: This is because they say, “The Fire will not touch us except for a few days.” They have been deceived in their faith by their wishful lying
phrases.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ لَن تَمَسَّنَا ٱلنَّارُ إِلَّآ أَيَّامٗا مَّعۡدُودَٰتٖۖ وَغَرَّهُمۡ فِي دِينِهِم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ
phrases.explanation: This is because they say the Fire will not touch us except for a few days, and they have been deceived in their faith by their wishful lying. The passage explains that these people, summoned to the Book of Allah to judge between them over their dispute with the Messenger, refused to heed the judgment of the Torah because they said the Fire would touch them only for counted days, namely forty days, the days of the calf worship, a delusion fabricated in their claim to be the sons of Allah and His beloved, and that Allah had promised their father Jacob that none of his offspring would enter the Fire save briefly. Allah declared them liars and told His Prophet that they are the inhabitants of the Fire abiding eternally, unlike the believers.

phrases.translation: But how ˹horrible˺ will it be when We gather them together on the Day about which there is no doubt—when every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged
phrases.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا جَمَعۡنَٰهُمۡ لِيَوۡمٖ لَّا رَيۡبَ فِيهِ وَوُفِّيَتۡ كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ مَّا كَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
phrases.explanation: But how horrible will it be when We gather them together on the Day about which there is no doubt, when every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged. How will it be asks in what state these people will be who turned from the Book of Allah and fabricated lies, a severe threat and warning. The verse means how tremendous their punishment will be when He gathers them for a Day on which every person is paid in full his recompense without wrong, and no creature fears any wrong or diminution. Paid in full means his good and evil, and not wronged means the doer of good is not deprived of his reward nor the doer of evil punished beyond his own misdeed.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O Allah! Lord over all authorities! You give authority to whoever You please and remove it from who You please;
phrases.ar: قُلِ ٱللَّهُمَّ مَٰلِكَ ٱلۡمُلۡكِ تُؤۡتِي ٱلۡمُلۡكَ مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَنزِعُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ مِمَّن
phrases.explanation: Say, O Allah, Lord over all authorities, You give authority to whoever You please and remove it from who You please. Say, O Prophet, means: say, O Allah. O Possessor of sovereignty means: O You to whom the sovereignty of this world and the Hereafter purely belongs, to the exclusion of anyone whomsoever at all. By You give sovereignty to whom You will is meant that You give sovereignty to whom You will, cause him to possess it and set him in authority over whom You will. By You take sovereignty away from whom You will is meant that You take it from whom You will to take it, the object being omitted as understood, as one says take what you will, meaning take what you will to take, just as in whatever form He willed He assembled you, meaning in whatever form He willed to assemble you. Some held that sovereignty in this place means prophethood.

phrases.translation: You honour whoever You please and disgrace who You please—all good is in Your Hands. Surely You ˹alone˺ are Most Capable of everything
phrases.ar: تَشَآءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَن تَشَآءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَآءُۖ بِيَدِكَ ٱلۡخَيۡرُۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٞ
phrases.explanation: You honour whoever You please and disgrace who You please, all good is in Your Hands, surely You alone are Most Capable of everything. To honour whom You will means to give him sovereignty and authority and extend power for him, and to disgrace whom You will means to strip him of his sovereignty and set his enemy in authority over him. In Your hand is all good means all of this is in Your hand and with You, and no one besides You has the power to do it, for You have power over all things, unlike the false gods that the polytheists among the People of the Book and the unlettered Arabs took as lords and worshipped instead of You, such as the Messiah and those set on a par with him.

phrases.translation: You cause the night to pass into the day and the day into the night.
phrases.ar: تُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِي ٱلَّيۡلِۖ
phrases.explanation: You cause the night to pass into the day and the day into the night. By You make pass is meant You make enter, from the verb meaning to enter a dwelling. By You make the night pass into the day is meant that You make what You have diminished of the hours of the night enter into the hours of the day, adding by the diminution of one to the increase of the other, and likewise You make what You have diminished of the day enter into the hours of the night, adding to the night what You diminished of the day. Thus the day lengthens as the night shortens, and the reverse.

phrases.translation: You bring forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living.
phrases.ar: وَتُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡحَيَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمَيِّتِ وَتُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡمَيِّتَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَيِّۖ
phrases.explanation: You bring forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living. The exegetes differed over this: some said the living thing is brought forth from the dead sperm-drop and the dead sperm-drop from the living thing, others said the date-palm from the date-stone and the date-stone from the date-palm, the grain from the ear and the ear from the grain, the egg from the hen and the hen from the egg, and others said the believer from the unbeliever and the unbeliever from the believer. The preferred view is that He brings forth the living human, livestock and animals from the dead sperm-drops, which is the living from the dead, and brings forth the dead sperm-drop from the living human, livestock and animals, which is the dead from the living. The reciters also differed over the vowel of the word for the dead: the intensified form covers what has not yet died but will die as well as what has already died, while the lightened form is only what has already died, and when the Arabs intend the adjectival sense they use the intensified pattern, so the intensified reading is more powerful in praise, since Allah brings forth the living from the sperm-drop already emitted, which is dead, and the dead sperm-drop from the living man before its emission, which is living.

phrases.translation: And You provide for whoever You will without limit.”
phrases.ar: وَتَرۡزُقُ مَن تَشَآءُ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابٖ
phrases.explanation: And You provide for whoever You will without limit. By it is meant that He gives to whom He wills of His creatures and is bountiful to him, without reckoning on His part with whom He has given, because He does not fear that diminution will occur in His treasuries or that what is in His hand will perish. All these things are in Your hand, the power by which You perform them, and no one besides You has power over them. The verse thus closes on the sovereignty of the previous verse: in Your hand is the good, indeed You have power over all things, and not to any whom the apostates claimed to be a god or took as a partner besides You.

phrases.translation: Believers should not take disbelievers as guardians instead of the believers—and whoever does so will have nothing to hope for from Allah—unless it is a precaution against their tyranny.
phrases.ar: لَّا يَتَّخِذِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَۖ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ فَلَيۡسَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ فِي شَيۡءٍ إِلَّآ أَن تَتَّقُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ تُقَىٰةٗۗ
phrases.explanation: Believers should not take disbelievers as guardians instead of the believers, and whoever does so will have nothing to hope for from Allah, unless it is a precaution against their tyranny. This is a prohibition from Allah to the believers against taking the unbelievers as helpers, allies and supporters. Do not take them as support or assist them against the Muslims while clinging to their religion. Whoever does that belongs to Allah in nothing, meaning he and Allah are cut off from each other through his apostasy and entry into unbelief. The exception, except that you guard yourselves against them out of precaution, means except when you are under their authority and fear them for your lives, so that you show them loyalty with your tongues while concealing enmity in your hearts, and you do not assist their unbelief nor help them against a Muslim in any deed. Others took the exception as kinship, but the preferred view is fearing them with fear, the precaution being only against the unbelievers. The reciters differed over the vowel of precaution, most reading tuqatan, the preferred recitation, established by widespread transmission.

phrases.translation: And Allah warns you about Himself. And to Allah is the final return
phrases.ar: وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسَهُۥۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
phrases.explanation: And Allah warns you about Himself, and to Allah is the final return. Allah makes you fear Himself, so that you commit no disobedience toward Him and take none of His enemies as protectors. With Allah is your return and your final destination after death, on the day of your gathering for the reckoning. When you return to Him having opposed His command and done what He forbade, namely taking the unbelievers as protectors in place of the believers, the punishment of your Lord will befall you that you cannot endure. So fear Him for your own sake and beware of Him, for He is severe in punishment.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, it is known to Allah.
phrases.ar: قُلۡ إِن تُخۡفُواْ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمۡ أَوۡ تُبۡدُوهُ يَعۡلَمۡهُ
phrases.explanation: Say, whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, it is known to Allah. The passage says this to those who were commanded not to take the unbelievers as allies in place of the believers. If you conceal in your hearts friendly loyalty toward the unbelievers and keep it secret, or reveal it with your tongues, deeds and actions and make it visible, Allah knows it, and nothing of it remains hidden from Him. So harbor no affection for them and show them no loyalty, for then the punishment of your Lord will befall you, what you cannot bear, because He knows your concealment and your openness and records it against you, requiting good with good and evil with the like of it.

phrases.translation: For He knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is Most Capable of everything.”
phrases.ar: ٱللَّهُۗ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٞ
phrases.explanation: And He knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is Most Capable of everything. Since nothing that is in a heaven or on an earth, or wherever it may be, remains hidden from Him, how then could what is in your hearts of inclination toward the unbelievers with affection and love, or what you show them of help in deed and word, remain hidden from Him. And Allah is Most Capable of everything means He has the power to punish you swiftly for your loyalty to them and your support of them against the believers, and for whatever He wills of matters, for nothing He intends is impossible for Him and nothing He desires is inaccessible to Him.

phrases.translation: ˹Watch for˺ the Day when every soul will be presented with whatever good it has done. And it will wish that its misdeeds were far off.
phrases.ar: يَوۡمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ مَّا عَمِلَتۡ مِنۡ خَيۡرٖ مُّحۡضَرٗا وَمَا عَمِلَتۡ مِن سُوٓءٖ تَوَدُّ لَوۡ أَنَّ بَيۡنَهَا وَبَيۡنَهُۥٓ أَمَدَۢا
phrases.explanation: Watch for the Day when every soul will be presented with whatever good it has done, and it will wish that its misdeeds were far off. Allah warns you of Himself on a Day when every soul will find the good it has done present and fully brought forth, and whatever evil it has done, it will wish that there were a far distance between itself and that evil, a far-removed final goal. Your destination on that Day is to Him, so fear Him for your own sake on account of your sins. Grammatically, the word for what standing with the verb has the meaning of that which, because the verb passes over to it transitively, and the second mention of what it has done of evil is coupled to the first.

phrases.translation: And Allah warns you about Himself. And Allah is Ever Gracious to ˹His˺ servants
phrases.ar: بَعِيدٗاۗ وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسَهُۥۗ وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
phrases.explanation: And a far distance, and Allah warns you about Himself, and Allah is Ever Gracious to His servants. Allah warns you of Himself: do not anger Him by committing what angers Him, so that you would meet Him on the Day when every soul finds its good present and wishes a far distance from its evil while He is wrathful with you, and His painful punishment befalls you that you cannot endure. Then He made known that He is full of compassion toward His servants and merciful to them, and part of His compassion is that He warns them of Himself, instills in them fear of His punishment, and forbids them the acts of disobedience to Him.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “If you ˹sincerely˺ love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive your sins. For Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
phrases.ar: قُلۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُحِبُّونَ ٱللَّهَ فَٱتَّبِعُونِي يُحۡبِبۡكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ
phrases.explanation:
Say, O Prophet, to the delegation of the Christians of Najran: if you truly love Allah, as you claim in your statements about Jesus, then follow me if you are truthful, for that is the sign of your truthfulness, since you know I am a messenger of Allah to you just as Jesus was. If you follow me and believe what I bring from Allah, He will love you, forgive your sins, and remit their punishment. He is Forgiving toward the sins of His believing servants and Merciful toward all His creatures.

The exegetes differed over the occasion: some said it was revealed about a people who claimed to love their Lord, others about the delegation of Najran. The preferred view is the latter, because elsewhere in this surah only that delegation is spoken of.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Obey Allah and His Messenger.” If they still turn away, then truly Allah does not like the disbelievers
phrases.ar: قُلۡ أَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَۖ فَإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
phrases.explanation: Say, O Prophet, to that same delegation of the Christians of Najran: obey Allah and His Messenger, for you have known with certainty that he is My messenger to My creation, that I sent him with the truth, and that you find him recorded with you in the Gospel. If they turn away from what you invite them to and turn their backs upon it, then make known to them that Allah does not love whoever disbelieves by denying a truth he has recognized and knew, and that they are among such deniers through their denial of your prophethood and of the truth upon which you stand, after they have known the validity of your affair and the reality of your prophethood.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of ’Imrân above all people ˹of their time˺
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ وَنُوحٗا وَءَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَءَالَ عِمۡرَٰنَ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
phrases.explanation: By "Indeed, Allah chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran above all people," He means that He selected Adam and Noah on account of their religion, and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran on account of the religion upon which they were, for they were the people of Islam. Thus He chose the religion of those He mentioned over all other religions that opposed it. By "the family of a man" is meant his followers, his people, and whoever is upon his religion, so the verse speaks of the households that followed these chosen ones, not only of the chosen persons themselves.

phrases.translation: They are descendants of one another. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.ar: ذُرِّيَّةَۢ بَعۡضُهَا مِنۢ بَعۡضٖۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
phrases.explanation: By "a progeny, one part of it descended from the other," He means that Allah chose the house of Abraham and the house of Imran, a progeny one part of which proceeded from the other. Grammatically, "progeny" is in the accusative either by separation from the definite "house of Imran," since "progeny" is indefinite, or by a repetition of "the choosing." In meaning, it refers only to their mutual alliance in religion and support in Islam, so their religion is one and their creed is one in the oneness of Allah and obedience to Him. And "Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing" means He hears the utterance of the wife of Imran and knows what she concealed when she vowed what was in her womb to Him as a consecrated offering.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when the wife of ’Imrân said, “My Lord! I dedicate what is in my womb entirely to Your service, so accept it from me. You ˹alone˺ are truly the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”
phrases.ar: إِذۡ قَالَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتُ عِمۡرَٰنَ رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرۡتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطۡنِي مُحَرَّرٗا فَتَقَبَّلۡ مِنِّيٓۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
phrases.explanation:
The word "when" is connected back to "All-Hearing" in the previous verse: Allah hears the utterance of the wife of Imran and knows what she concealed. She was Hanna, wife of Imran.

By "My Lord, I have dedicated to You what is in my womb, set free," she means: I have vowed that what is in my womb belongs to You, set free for Your worship and the service of Your sanctuary, dedicated exclusively to You. "Set free" is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier. "So accept it from me" means: accept what I have promised You. "Truly, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing" means: You hear what I say and know what I intend, so nothing of my affair is hidden from You.

phrases.translation: When she delivered, she said, “My Lord! I have given birth to a
phrases.ar: فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتۡهَا قَالَتۡ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعۡتُهَآ
phrases.explanation: By "she bore her" is meant: she brought her forth, as one says "the woman gave birth, she gives birth, with the giving birth." The reciters differed over this word. Most read "she bore," as a report from Allah that He is the Knower of what she bore, separate from her own statement, "My Lord, I have given birth to her, a female." Some of the earlier scholars read "and Allah knows best what I bore," as a report from the mother of Mary about herself. The preferred view is the reading transmitted by widespread and compelling transmission, which is clear and not refuted: "and Allah knows best what she bore."

phrases.translation: girl,”—and Allah fully knew what she had delivered—“and the male is not like the female.
phrases.ar: أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتۡ وَلَيۡسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلۡأُنثَىٰۖ وَإِنِّي سَمَّيۡتُهَا
phrases.explanation: The explanation is then: Allah knows, better than all His creatures, what she bore. He then returned to reporting her statement, for she was excusing herself to her Lord for what she had promised and consecrated during her pregnancy for the service of her Lord: "and the male is not like the female," because the male is stronger in the service and performs it better, and because the female in some conditions is not fit to enter the sanctuary and perform the service of the church there, on account of what befalls her of menstruation and postpartum bleeding. "And I have named her Mary," as she said.

phrases.translation: I have named her Mary, and I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed.”
phrases.ar: مَرۡيَمَ وَإِنِّيٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ
phrases.explanation: By her statement "I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed," she means: I make her, and the refuge of her offspring from the accursed Satan, with You. That is, she asks Allah to be the refuge of Mary and of Mary's descendants against the accursed Satan. She had already named the child Mary, and now she commends both the girl and her future offspring to Allah's protection, since she had vowed the child to the service of the sanctuary and wished it kept safe from all harm, and from every whisper, touch, and harm of Satan, so that she may grow up in Your protection and service.

phrases.translation: So her Lord accepted her graciously and blessed her with a pleasant upbringing—entrusting
phrases.ar: فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٖ وَأَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا
phrases.explanation: By "So her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance," He means that Allah accepted Mary from her mother Hanna, together with her vow dedicating her to the service of the temple and of her Lord. Grammatically, "acceptance" is a verbal noun that is not rendered in the form of its verb, which would be "with a goodly accepting." The Arabs often do this, rendering verbal nouns in the root-form of the verb even when the verb is augmented, as in their saying "so-and-so spoke a word" instead of "spoke a speaking." The same applies to "and He made her grow with a goodly growth," where He did not say "with a goodly growing."

phrases.translation: her to the care of Zachariah. Whenever Zachariah visited her in the sanctuary, he found her supplied with provisions. He exclaimed, “O Mary! Where did this come from?” She replied, “It is from Allah. Surely Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit.”
phrases.ar: حَسَنٗا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّاۖ كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيۡهَا زَكَرِيَّا ٱلۡمِحۡرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزۡقٗاۖ قَالَ يَٰمَرۡيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَٰذَاۖ قَالَتۡ هُوَ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرۡزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابٍ
phrases.explanation:
The reciters differed over "and He made Zachariah her guardian." Most of the reciters of the Hijaz, Medina, and Basra read it with a light consonant, "and he made her his own," citing the verse "which of them would be guardian of Mary." Most of the reciters of Kufa read it with a doubled consonant, "and Allah made Zachariah her guardian." The preferred view is the doubled reading: Allah made Zachariah her guardian, that is, He joined her to him. He joined her to himself only because Allah had joined her to him, by His decree in his favor when they disputed over her. It is reported that Zachariah and his opponents, when they contended over which of them she should reside with, cast lots by throwing their reed shafts into the river Jordan. Some said his shaft remained fixed and stood upright while the water carried the others away, others that his shaft rose up while the rest drifted with the current. Whichever it was, it was a sign from Allah that he was most deserving of her, a decree of Allah assigning her to him over his opponents. The argument of those who read the light form from the verse about guardianship of Mary actually points to the weakness of their reasoning.

The reciters also differed over the name "Zachariah," some of Medina lengthening it and most of Kufa shortening it. Both are well-known, widespread readings among the Muslims, with no contradiction between them, so either recitation is correct. When it is lengthened, it stands in the accusative without case-ending, being a foreign name that is not inflected, and this goes with the doubled reading of "guardian."

Others disagreed about how he became her guardian, saying he became so after Hanna gave birth to Mary, without any casting of lots or dispute, because her mother died after her father while she was still a child, and the wife of Zachariah was her maternal aunt. It has also been said that the name of the mother of John, the aunt of Jesus, was Elizabeth.

By "every time Zachariah entered the prayer-niche to her, he found with her provision," He means that every time he entered the niche after leading her into it, he found provision from Allah there for her nourishment. Others said he found an abundance of provision beyond what he brought her, with which he maintained her in those days. The "prayer-niche" is the foremost part of every place of prayer, the most elevated and noblest of them, and so it is also with mosques. He said, "O Mary, whence have you this?" meaning: from which direction does this provision come to you that I see with you? Mary answered, "It is from Allah," meaning that it is Allah who granted her that provision, conveyed it to her, and gave it to her. Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit.

phrases.translation: Then and there Zachariah prayed to his Lord, saying, “My Lord! Grant
phrases.ar: هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُۥۖ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبۡ
phrases.explanation: "There Zakariyyah prayed to his Lord" means: at that moment, when Zachariah saw with Mary what he saw of Allah's provision for her, and the favor He bestowed on her without any human being being a cause of it, and when he beheld with her the fresh, ripe fruit that was not customarily found on the earth at the time he saw it. Then he desired a child despite his advanced age and the barrenness of his wife, hoping that Allah would grant him a child from her despite their condition, just as He provided for Mary when she had withdrawn from the people, with summer fruits in winter and winter fruits in summer. So he turned to Allah, longing for a child, and asked Him for a goodly offspring.

phrases.translation: me—by your grace—righteous offspring.
phrases.ar: لِي مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةٗ طَيِّبَةًۖ
phrases.explanation: By "grant me from Your presence a goodly offspring," He means: grant me from with You, that is, a gift from Your presence with Yourself. By "offspring" He means the descendants, and by "goodly" the blessed. So he asks not merely for any child but for a blessed lineage granted directly from Allah. He says "from Your presence" to stress that the gift comes from Allah alone, with no partner and no human cause, just as the provision He gave Mary came from Him alone. The hope is that the child and all those after him would be righteous, blessed, and of benefit to His religion and to His servants.

phrases.translation: You are certainly the Hearer of ˹all˺ prayers.”
phrases.ar: إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ
phrases.explanation: By "indeed, You are the Hearer of all prayers," He means: indeed, You are the One who hears the supplication. The word "Hearer" is more laudatory than "hearer," and it carries the meaning of the One who responds to it. The verse is therefore: at that moment Zachariah called upon his Lord and said, "My Lord, grant me from with You a blessed child, indeed You are the One who responds to the supplication of whoever calls upon You." In short, he addressed his Lord with a prayer for a goodly offspring and affirmed that Allah hears and answers every supplication made to Him with sincerity and need.

phrases.translation: So the angels called out to him while he stood praying in the sanctuary, “Allah gives you good news of ˹the birth
phrases.ar: فَنَادَتۡهُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَهُوَ قَآئِمٞ يُصَلِّي فِي ٱلۡمِحۡرَابِ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ
phrases.explanation: The angels called out to him while he stood praying in the sanctuary. "While he was standing" reports the time of the call: they called to Zachariah in the state of standing in prayer, and "praying" describes his standing. The reciters differed over "the angels called": most read it in the feminine, meaning the collective body of the angels, while some of Kufa read it in the masculine, meaning Gabriel called to him. Both are well-known readings with no difference in meaning, so either is correct. Most also read "that Allah gives you good news" with a fatha on "that," because the call falls upon it, while some read a kasra citing an early reading, a ground that is invalid because the vocative stands between.

phrases.translation: of˺ John who will confirm the Word of
phrases.ar: بِيَحۡيَىٰ مُصَدِّقَۢا بِكَلِمَةٖ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ
phrases.explanation: "Of John": the name comes from the saying "he lived, so he is John," and it is said that Allah named him with it because his name is interpreted as "He made him live through faith." "Who will confirm the Word of Allah": by "confirming a word from Allah" He means Jesus the son of Mary, so John will confirm the truth of Jesus. Grammatically, "confirming" is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier describing John, since it is a state of John. Some scholars of Arabic from Basra claimed another sense for "word," but the interpretation is that Allah gives you, O Zachariah, glad tidings of John as a son for you, one who confirms a word from Allah, that is, Jesus the son of Mary, and the interpreters spoke in accordance with this. The exegetes differed over the report of who said what on this point, but the meaning stands as described.

phrases.translation: Allah and will be a great leader, chaste, and a prophet among the righteous.”
phrases.ar: وَسَيِّدٗا وَحَصُورٗا وَنَبِيّٗا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
phrases.explanation: "And will be a great leader": "leader" means a noble one in knowledge and worship, from the verb meaning "he led," and it is in the accusative by conjunction to "confirming." "Chaste" means abstaining from intercourse with women, from the verb meaning "I prevented," and it is also recited in another form. One who does not reveal his secret and conceals it is also called "chaste," because he holds it back, and the origin of all these meanings is preventing and holding in. "And a prophet among the righteous" means a messenger from his Lord to his people, who informs them of Him and of what He has sent, and "from the righteous" means from His righteous prophets. Prophethood and its origin have already been explained earlier in this commentary, with the proofs for it, so He describes John as confirming the Word, a leader, chaste, and a prophet of the righteous.

phrases.translation: Zachariah exclaimed, “My Lord! How can I have a son when I am very old and my wife is barren?” He replied, “So will it be. Allah does what He wills.”
phrases.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلَٰمٞ وَقَدۡ بَلَغَنِيَ ٱلۡكِبَرُ وَٱمۡرَأَتِي عَاقِرٞۖ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ ٱللَّهُ يَفۡعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ
phrases.explanation: When the angels called to him that Allah gives him glad tidings of John, Zachariah said: "My Lord! How can I have a son when I am very old and my wife is barren?" By this he means: whoever has reached the age I have reached no longer has children, and my wife is barren. "Old age" is the verbal noun of "he grows old." By "So will it be. Allah does what He wills," He means: He is as He has described Himself, for it is easy for Him to create a child from the aged one who has despaired of a child and from the barren one, just as He created you, O Zachariah, before creating the child from you, when you were nothing. For nothing He wills is impossible for Him.

phrases.translation: Zachariah said, “My Lord! Grant me
phrases.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَل لِّيٓ
phrases.explanation: This is a report about Zachariah. He said: "My Lord, grant me a sign," meaning: if this call with which I was called, and the voice I heard, is the voice of Your angels and a glad tiding from You to me, then grant me a sign, that is, a mark, that it is indeed so, so that what the devil whispered into my heart may fall away from me, namely that this was the voice of something other than the angels. The "sign" is the mark, whose meaning was explained earlier. The reciters differed over the word "sign": some said its glottal stop was dropped because the doubling was burdensome, while others said its first letter was changed to a plain letter, as with "need" and "stature."

phrases.translation: a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not ˹be able to˺ speak to people for three
phrases.ar: ءَايَةٗۖ قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَٰثَةَ
phrases.explanation: "A sign. He said, your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days..." According to what has been transmitted, Allah punished him for asking for a sign after the angels had already conveyed the glad tidings to him orally. He made his sign a confirmation that what he had heard from the angels about John was from Allah, a mark that combined what he had asked for with a purification of his slip in asking. The exegetes differed over "except by gestures": some said it means moving the lips without forming speech with the tongue, while others said it means beckoning with the hand or head without speaking.

phrases.translation: days except through gestures. Remember your Lord often and glorify ˹Him˺ morning and evening.”
phrases.ar: أَيَّامٍ إِلَّا رَمۡزٗاۗ وَٱذۡكُر رَّبَّكَ كَثِيرٗا وَسَبِّحۡ بِٱلۡعَشِيِّ وَٱلۡإِبۡكَٰرِ
phrases.explanation: Days pass with the sign of not speaking to people except through gestures. "And remember your Lord often and glorify Him morning and evening." Allah said to Zachariah: your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gestures, without muteness, defect, or illness. And remember your Lord much, for nothing will prevent you from remembering Him or from glorifying Him. By "in the evening" He means: glorify your Lord by His worship in the evening. "Early morning" is the going out for a need in the period between the rising of the dawn and the time of the forenoon. So he was to remember Allah much and to glorify Him in the evening and in the early morning, day and night, and to call upon Him in every state.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when the angels said, “O Mary! Surely
phrases.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَتِ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرۡيَمُ إِنَّ
phrases.explanation: "And remember when the angels said, O Mary! Indeed..." This connects back to the previous verses, where Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing of the vow of the wife of Imran. Now the angels address Mary directly and begin their address with the word "Indeed," to confirm what follows about her.
